newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq up on demerger speculation.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq up on demerger speculation.

text.p: Shares in Allied Domecq Plc touched a five-month high on Friday amid talk that the company may raise the prospect of a demerger of its spirits arm when it reports full-year results next Tuesday, traders and analysts said.

Any remarks from Allied about restructuring, especially a demerger of the spirits unit, would be greeted positively by the investment community, which sees it as a way for the group to reverse its relatively poor performance in the sector.
The stock was up 16p at 492 by 1158 GMT in active trade of 3.4 million shares. Earlier it reached a day's high of 493p -- its highest since the end of May.
"Obviously people are hoping there will be some news on a demerger," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
"The market is looking for a demerger or at least some clarification on strategy," said another.
"A trading demerger would really add value to the group, the City has obviously done its sums and worked out it is worth about 5 pounds on a post-demerger basis."
Allied Domecq's spirits and wine division includes brands such as Ballantine's whisky, Beefeater gin, Canadian Club Whisky and Tia Maria liquer.

A number of analysts have turned more positive on the stock since the company sold its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass in August. "The reason people have been turning positive is because of the expectation of change at the company rather than because of the figures, which are going to be unexciting," said Colin Humphreys, analyst at Panmure Gordon.
"There is an expectation that things must change because the company has so clearly not done well over the last few years. It is straightforward market speculation," Humpreys said.
-- David Holmes and Tim Farrand, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 5106
